transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Riya (CSM) -- Liam, Sofia, Ethan, Hannah (VeraSafe)

Summary: quick sync to confirm commitment uplift, EU on‑prem pilot readiness and timeline.

00:00 Liam O'Connor: okay thanks everyone for jumping on, we wanted to walk through the last readout from legal and ops and make sure we're aligned on timing for the top up.
00:12 Maya (Redwood AE): yep, thanks Liam. quick agenda — confirm capacity numbers, go over EU on‑prem checklist, and then Jordan will talk perf expectations and the soak test.
00:24 Sofia Mendes: before we start — high level constraint, our PCI-ish environment means we need the model serving inside our EU cluster and KMS integrated with HSM. can we do that with Redwood Private?
00:35 Jordan (Redwood SE): 100% — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. on the on‑prem package we have a KMS adaptor and audit log forwarding; Ethan we can share the architecture diagram after this call.
00:47 Ethan Park: perfect, also we need SAML SSO for the console and RBAC to be enforced by roles, not just service tokens.
00:55 Riya (CSM): we provision SSO via SAML and map groups to RBAC, we can include that mapping in the runbook.
01:05 Hannah Li: timeline question — legal wants to see SOC2 and data retention policy. do you have the most recent SOC2?
01:13 Maya: yes, we'll attach the SOC2 Type II and ISO evidence; also we'll include the retention and deletion docs. I'll drop all artifacts into the shared folder.
01:22 Liam: cool. on capacity - our product team is forecasting a 2.5x peak uplift in Q2 with sustained 1.6x baseline. we're targeting a lift of 60 vGPU-hours per day initially, then scale. can you confirm pricing tiers if we commit to reserved capacity?
01:35 Maya: for reserved capacity we can provide a tier discount starting at the 3‑month commit. I've noted the numbers from procurement; I'll push a pricing worksheet. provisional numbers look like a 22% effective discount at the 12‑month uplift, but we'll confirm.
01:49 Sofia: latency SLO for fraud model is 120ms p95. can we hit that in the on‑prem setup given our sequence lengths?
01:58 Jordan: depends on the model and quantization. for the family you're using (open-llm-fair-8b variant) we typically see 60–110ms p95 on an A100-equivalent in local private mode with continuous batching tuned. KV cache warmup is key; we'll provide warmup scripts. caveat — if you increase batch sizes for throughput p95 will shift.
02:22 Ethan: what's the fallback for capacity loss? we run a critical path for fraud detection and can't have gaps.
02:31 Jordan: you can enable smart routing to fallback to hosted Redwood in another region — but since this is a sovereignty requirement, fallback would only be to a dedicated private replica in another EU cluster, not the hosted public. we can also set circuit-breaker style throttles and local queueing.
02:50 Liam: procurement asked about audit logs and retention — do you stream logs to customer SIEM?
02:58 Maya: yes, we support syslog/EC2 forwarders and can push audit events to your SIEM. logs are configurable for retention on the private plane.
03:10 Hannah: on onboarding, what is the activation lead time? ops wants a fast window, ideally 3 weeks from PO.
03:19 Riya: typical on‑prem lead time is 2–6 weeks depending on hardware and network prep — if you have infra ready, 3 weeks is achievable. we need IP allowlist, firewall opening, and KMS key rotation policy details.
03:33 Sofia: hardware — are you prescriptive on GPU types? we prefer a mix of 80GB to support long contexts for investigations.
03:41 Jordan: we recommend 80GB A100s or H100s for 32k seqs; if you're doing quantized 8-bit, 40GB with nvlink can be enough but perf varies. we'll propose a config for the pilot.
03:58 Liam: about the soak test, we want a 2-week window with a controlled traffic replay. can Redwood run the benchmark with our harness or do we need to run it?
04:08 Jordan: we can run it jointly. Jordan + your SRE will run replays using your harness, and we'll instrument traces. deliverable: perf report with p50/p95/p99, token cost, and suggested batching settings.
04:25 Sofia: are there any gotchas with KV cache in warm-up? we've seen cold starts be expensive.
04:32 Jordan: yep — prefix caching and persistent KV between requests helps. we'll ship a warmup script that hits common prefixes and maintains cache. also recommend gradual rollout during soak to ramp caches.
04:46 Liam: security — we need KMS key rotation, customer-controlled keys, and no plaintext token storage.
04:53 Ethan: and we want HSM-backed keys.
04:56 Maya: supported — Redwood Private can be configured to use your HSM via our KMS connector. we'll include the connector guide.
05:05 Hannah: any contractual changes for on‑prem? our legal asked about indemnity and SLA credits for private.
05:12 Maya: SLA model differs for Private. we'll share the private SLA addendum; credits for downtime can be negotiated in the statement of work.
05:22 Liam: great. circling back to capacity numbers — can you provision a small burst pool for flash events? e.g., 30% extra burst for 48h windows?
05:32 Jordan: yes, burst pools are supported; for private deployments we can pre-stage a burst node pool or reserve capacity in a dedicated pool. cost depends on reserved vs on-demand.
05:43 Sofia: last question — observability. do we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards in the private UI?
05:51 Riya: yes, the console mirrors hosted: token-level billing, per-model tracing, alerts and rollouts. we can set retention to your spec.
06:02 Liam: ok, sounds good. next steps recap?
06:08 Maya: I'll attach SOC2, the private deployment runbook, the pricing worksheet, and the EU activation checklist by Friday (2027-02-12). Jordan will schedule the perf window and send the warmup script by Monday. Ethan to provide IP ranges and KMS contact by Tuesday.
06:24 Ethan: noted.
06:27 Hannah: we want a joint run for the soak test starting 2027-02-21 if all approvals are done.
06:33 Maya: works — we'll block time and prep the bench harness.
06:36 Liam: thanks everyone.
06:38 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some names mangled by auto-transcribe; minor word swaps (K V cash vs KV cache) in places.
